taxonomy:
## Taxonomy (by core mechanic), using only the provided rules

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black/edge; bulbs can’t illuminate each other; each white cell illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color black cells so each number equals the count of white cells from the number to the nearest black cell or frame (horizontally+vertically); numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.

### B) Black/white (or shaded/unshaded) region formation
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; orthogonally connected black cells must form rectangles/squares; orthogonally connected white cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give size of the area containing the cell.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms (bold rectangle regions) with numbers = count of painted cells; white cells can’t stretch across more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.
- **Hitori**: No number repeats in any row/column among white cells; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-enclosed territories have numbers indicating how many more marks they get; “—” and “|” have max extension constraints (horizontal/vertical limits).
- **Kurotto**: Color some cells black; circle number = sum of continuous black cells extending from it (orthogonally); empty circles may have any number; circle cells can’t be colored.
- **LITS**: In each bold area, color four consecutive squares (tetromino); similarly shaped tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares form a connected network; no 2×2 or larger all-colored squares.
- **Nurikabe**: Fill with black/white; numbers indicate size of continuous white regions; each white region has exactly one number; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nurimeizu**: Shade cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Nuritwin**: Shade some cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells connected across boundaries; blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms (bold regions) have a number = count of continuous black cells in that room; rooms with no number any; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; after “dropping” stones straight down, stones must fill bottom half with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-enclosed tiles are colored; diagonal-line cell number gives required count of black cells to the right or downward along that line/column until grid edge or another diagonal-number cell; all cells of a tile are either all colored or all uncolored; final solution shows outline of an object.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; cells containing numbers cannot be colored; (additional constraints are implied by the provided rules: colored cells cannot connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells; and each rectangle bordered by bold lines has exactly one wrong number—this is part of the provided rules for Usowan.)

### C) Loop / path drawing (single non-self-crossing loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers orthogonally; no crossing/branching/revisiting; must pass all white circles; in each bold-enclosed area, loop either goes straight through all white circles or turns right-angled at all of them; must not pass black circles.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; passes all circles; white circles require straight-through and a right-angled turn in at least one adjacent cell; black circles require a right-angled turn at the circle cell then straight through next cell.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; passes through arrow cells; loop direction is determined by arrow directions; wind constraints prevent moving against wind and restrict entering/bending near borders/black cells.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop through cell centers orthogonally; no crossing/branching/revisiting; must pass all black circles with each black circle as midpoint of the straight segment through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; each bold room visited exactly once; in each room loop goes through all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); after moons in one room, next room entered must be suns, and vice versa.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms (bold regions) each contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicated in a row/column, distance between duplicates must be ≥ that number.
- **Slitherlink**: Connect adjacent dots with vertical/horizontal lines to make a single loop; numbers indicate how many lines surround the cell; empty cells any; loop never crosses or branches.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; dotted segments between black cells or outer frame are “Gates”; loop must pass all gates but each gate only once; loop starts/returns to open numbered circle; open circle number = number of gates to go through; gate endpoint numbers indicate when loop crosses that gate (first crossed in a direction for “1”, etc.).
- **Yajilin**: Single loop through cell centers; no crossing/branching/revisiting; numbers show how many black cells in arrow direction; loop does not pass through black cells or number cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Yosenabe**: (Loop/path) Not a loop; instead circles move into gray areas with straight arrows. So it belongs elsewhere (see D).

### D) Movement / routing with directed constraints (not necessarily loops)
- **Nagareru**: Loop with wind direction constraints (also in C, but specifically direction/wind rules).
- **Satogaeri**: Move circles vertically/horizontally so each bold “country” contains exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; some circles without numbers may not move; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Yosenabe**: Move all circles orthogonally into gray areas; each move shown by an arrow whose tip is in a gray cell; arrows don’t bend and don’t cross other white circles or other arrows; number in a gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it; empty gray areas any sum but at least one circle must enter a gray area.

### E) Pairing / connection puzzles (paths between matching endpoints)
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges equal to the island number; max two bridges between two islands; bridges can’t cross islands/bridges; bridges form a continuous link between all islands.
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally or turning; never twice through same cell; lines can’t cross/branch off/go through number cells.
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils; draw lines from the tip through cell centers; pencil is a straight group of one or more cells with tip at one end; number in pencil cell gives pencil length; line from tip goes through one or as many cells as the number; line can’t cross itself or branch off.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares (four kinds); cannot place in black squares; uncovered white parts always form a rectangle or square; numbers indicate how many black triangles are around it orthogonally.
- **Yajilin**: (Loop-based, but also a “routing” constraint; already categorized in C.)

### F) Tiling / partitioning into blocks/regions with shape constraints
- **Chained Block**: Fill blocks of consecutive black cells; number indicates block size; “?” unknown; every block has one number or “?”; blocks in corner contact form chains; all blocks part of a chain; chain can’t contain more than one block of the same size/shape (rotation/mirror considered same).
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines over dotted lines; each block contains a pair of white-area and gray-area with same form (rotation/mirror allowed); number indicates total cells of that color in the block equals half the block’s cells; block can contain any number of cells with the number.
- **Evolomino**: Draw squares in some white cells; orthogonally connected group is a block; each block contains exactly one square placed on a pre-drawn arrow; each arrow path passes through at least two blocks; subsequent blocks on an arrow route add one square without rotating/flipping.
- **Five Cells**: Divide grid into blocks of five cells; no blocks with 0–4 or 6+ cells; numbers show how many lines of a block are around the cell (including outer frame); up to 5 numbered cells per block; lines must surround a cell and cannot enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill empty cells with numbers; divide board into blocks; each block filled with same number horizontally or vertically; each block contains as many cells as the number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (Not tiling; already in E.)
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**: (Region/block constraints; already in B.)
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles with numbers in cells; each rectangle contains only one number showing number of cells in rectangle.
- **Sashigane**: Divide grid into L-shaped blocks one block wide; all blocks must be L-shaped; open circles form the knee; open circle number = number of cells in its block; arrows point toward the knee; number of marks in a block (arrows or open circles) may be 0–3.
- **Tilepaint**: (Tile coloring; already in B.)
- **Sto-stone**: (Rooms; already in B.)
- **Suraromu**: (Loop with gates; already in C.)

### G) Arithmetic / counting constraints on grid cells (non-loop, non-tiling)
- **Choco Banana**: Numbers indicate size of the area containing the cell (also in B).
- **Kurodoko**: Numbers count white cells to nearest black cell or frame (also in A).
- **Kurotto**: Circle number = sum of continuous black cells extending from it (also in B).
- **Hebi**: Place numbers in snake parts so 1→5 sequentially connected; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; from 2→1 direction, other snake parts can’t be in squares next to black square or rim; black squares numbers show nearest square count in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Heyawake**: Numbers count painted cells in a room (also in B).
- **Juosan**: Territory numbers count additional marks (also in B).
- **Ripple Effect**: Room numbers consecutive; duplicated numbers distance constraint (also in C).
- **Satogaeri**: Circle numbers indicate how many cells to pass through (also in D).
- **Yosenabe**: Gray area numbers equal total of entering circle numbers (also in D).
- **Usowan**: Numbers show how many colored cells are next to a cell orthogonally, but each bold rectangle has exactly one wrong number (also in B).

### H) Sudoku / Latin-square style constraints
- **Sudoku**: Place numbers 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each 3×3 bold block contains all numbers 1–9.

### I) Pure “fill with numbers” / digit placement with local rules
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with numbers from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; one cell has only one digit.
- **Sudoku**: (already in H)

### J) “No-touch / connectivity” constraints (graph connectivity)
- **Hitori**: black cells never touch; white cells connected (also in B).
- **Kurodoko**: black cells can’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected (also in A).
- **Nurikabe**: black cells continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2 (also in B).
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**: shaded cells connected across boundaries; blocks can’t touch orthogonally (also in B).
- **LITS**: colored squares connected; no 2×2 all-colored (also in B).
- **Akari**: bulbs can’t illuminate other bulbs; every white cell illuminated (also in A).

If you want, I can also produce a second taxonomy that groups games by **output type** (bulbs/bridges/lines/shading/numbers) instead of by mechanic.
